newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Res Beijing Land ends at HK$4.05.
newsitem.headline: China Res Beijing Land ends at HK$4.05.

text.p: Shares of China Resources Beijing Land Ltd, the spinoff China property arm of China Resources Enterprise Ltd, ended their trading debut on Friday at HK$4.05 each, compared with the issue price of HK$2.36.
"Its strong China-backed parent and its red-chip concept brought about its strong performance," said ASG Investment analyst Michael Ng.
Red chips, or Hong Kong-incorporated firms with major backing from or connections with China, have been popular with investors in recent weeks.
The stock opened at HK$3.20 before covering a range from HK$3.00 to HK$4.075 during the day.
"Its price fared better than expected," said G.K. Goh Securities dealing manager Boby Ho, who had tipped a price range of HK$3.0-3.2. He said speculation accounted for much of the buying.
But Ng noted: "It is worth a buy in the longer term as its fundamentals are seen strong."
The stock chalked up a volume of 214.58 million shares as the heaviest traded counter of the day. It posted a turnover of HK$765.37 million.

China Resouces Beijing Land offered 300 million shares of which 15 percent of the issue was for public subscription in Hong Kong and 85 percent for placement to professioanl and institutional investors.
The Hong Kong flotation of shares of the company was 125.7 times subscribed.
The sole material asset of China Resources Beijing Land is its 62.5 percent equity interest in Beijing Huayuan Property Co Ltd, a land development and investment company in Beijing.
